designSummary: Strand 1: cohort of OPAT episodes with complication rates per 1,000 catheter days; strand 2: framework analysis of about 28 interviews; integration by joint display.
sampleSize: The 1,870 episodes are fixed. If about 12 percent have a complication requiring hospital contact, about 220 events are expected. With 220 events and a third of catheter days on midlines, a rate ratio of 1.5 between line types can be detected with about 80 percent power at two-sided alpha 0.05, and the model can carry about 11 parameters at 20 events per parameter. For strand 2, about 16 patients or carers and 12 nurses are planned by information power: a focused aim, a specific sample from the extremes and an established analysis framework; sampling stops early if no new explanations appear in three consecutive interviews.
primaryAnalysis: Poisson regression with robust standard errors for complication counts per episode, with the log of catheter days as offset, adjusted for eight pre-specified covariates (line type, lumens, vancomycin or vesicant, planned duration, indication, agency team, living alone, interpreter need); rates reported with 95 percent confidence intervals.
secondaryAnalysis: The same model for line-associated bloodstream infection if at least 20 events occur, otherwise descriptive counts; a sensitivity analysis adding home-managed complications if the agency notes are shared; framework analysis of interviews with two coders and a joint display.
missingData: Episodes with missing line type or dates are counted and described; line type missing in more than 5 percent of episodes triggers multiple imputation with 20 imputations; missing agency notes are reported as a limitation, never imputed.
multiplicity: One primary rate model; secondary outcomes are descriptive with confidence intervals.
software: R with the sandwich package for strand 1; NVivo for strand 2.
overfittingGuards: Interview sampling frame fixed from strand 1 results before any interview
summary: About 220 expected events support a rate ratio of 1.5 with about 80 percent power; about 28 interviews planned by information power.
